title: Count N-Queens Placements
statement: A chess coach wants to know how many safe drills she can set up. Given an integer n >= 1, return the number of distinct ways to place n queens on an n x n board so that no two queens share a row, a column, or a diagonal (either direction). Return a single integer count. If no placement is possible, return 0. Examples: n = 1 has 1 placement, n = 2 and n = 3 have 0, n = 4 has 2, and n = 8 has 92.
hints: Every valid placement has exactly one queen per row. What if you commit to a queen in row 0, then row 1, and so on, undoing a choice when it leads nowhere?
Track three conflict sets while you recurse: occupied columns, and the two diagonal families keyed by row - col and row + col. A square (row, col) is safe only if all three keys are free.

Recurse row by row: for each free column in the current row, add col, row - col, and row + col to the three sets, recurse on row + 1 (adding its returned count), then remove all three keys before trying the next column. When row == n you have one complete placement, so return 1.
